method: API evaluator 1.0: three caption-blind observers each received only the image inside the request; a coder, run 2 times, received only the contract and their answers split into numbered units and cited a unit for each finding; code verified every citation and computed the verdict, which passes only when every coding passes (scripts/lib/adjudication.mjs). AI review is not clinical approval.

observers.label: Caption-blind observer 1 (Claude)

answers.1: The side of a man's head and neck, seen in profile from behind/side. The hair on the side and back is shaved short, and the ear is fully visible. Four separate panels show the same view.
answers.2: Panel 1: a white cloth bandage wrapped around the head, tied in a small bow near the front, with a square white gauze pad sitting over the area just behind and above the ear. Panel 2: two hands at the back of the head holding the unwound end of the bandage, which now hangs loose; the pad is gone and the skin behind the ear is bare. Panel 3: no bandage; a thin curved line runs along the skin just behind the ear, following the ear's curve, with about four small white tape strips laid crosswise over it. Panel 4: a close-up through a magnifying glass of that same curved line behind the ear with four white tape strips across it.
answers.3: Dark circles with white numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 in the top-left of each panel, giving the order of steps. A teal arrow in panel 2, upper left, pointing left/backward, showing the direction to pull the bandage. A magnifying-glass shape in panel 4 with a white oval label reading "Check for tape" below it.
answers.4: Someone might read the curved line and strips as a fresh wound splitting open, or think the small tapes are stitches that must be pulled out.
answers.5: Untie and unwrap the head bandage, pulling the loose end backward (away from the face) to remove it along with the gauze pad from behind the ear, then look closely at the curved line behind the ear to check that the small tape strips are still in place. It does not say what to do if a tape is missing.

observers.label: Caption-blind observer 2 (Claude)

answers.1: A man's head and upper neck, seen from the side (left side profile, facing right). Panel 4 is a close-up circle, like a magnifying glass, over the area behind and around the ear.
answers.2: Panel 1: a white gauze bandage wrapped around the head, tied in a bow at the back, with a square white pad sitting over the ear area; the hair above is partly shaved. Panel 2: a hand at the back of the head holding the loose, untied end of the bandage, which now hangs down; the head band is still across the forehead. Panel 3: bandage gone; behind the ear there is a thin curved line along the hairline that looks like a stitched or glued cut, with several small pale strips laid across it. Panel 4: the same curved line behind the ear with four small tan/white tape strips crossing it, and the ear looks normal.
answers.3: Numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 in dark circles at the top left of each panel, giving the order of steps. A teal arrow in panel 2 at the upper left points left/backwards, showing the direction to pull the bandage. A label in an oval at the bottom of panel 4 reads "Check for tape".
answers.4: A worried patient might read it as an injury or bleeding wound behind the ear needing re-bandaging, rather than a routine dressing change.
answers.5: Untie the head bandage at the back, pull the loose end away/backwards to unwrap it, remove the pad, then look closely at the line behind the ear and check that the small tape strips are still in place.
